All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [0.16.0] - 2026-11-23

### Added

- **The emulated WhatsApp template records its name, language and params.**
  `GET /admin/emulator/outbox` entries for a template send now carry
  `contenido` as `[plantilla <name> (<lang>)] <p1> | <p2>` and a structured
  `plantilla: {nombre, idioma, params}` field (omitted for non-template
  sends). Before, only `[plantilla <name>]` was kept, so a proactive message
  could not be read in full in emulated environments. Real sending is
  untouched. The text form changed from `[plantilla <name>]` to include the
  language.

## [0.15.1] - 2026-11-23

### Changed

- **mvp registers the Instagram adapter in emulated mode.** The mvp overlay sets
  `herald-instagram-emulated-account` to `17841400000000001`, as dev already
  does. Without it mvp had no Instagram adapter at all (no app secret there), so
  no Instagram account could be emulated and MUSA's inbox couldn't be tested in
  mvp with no social network connected. Config only; turn it off the day mvp
  serves a real Instagram account.

## [0.15.0] - 2026-11-16

### Added

- **The `callback_url` forward carries the sender's phone.** The payload POSTed
  to a binding's `callback_url` now has `sender_phone` (the sender's verified
  phone, the same value Nexus receives as `sender_phone`; `""` when the channel
  doesn't know it) and `contact_shared` (true only when this very message is the
  sender's own shared contact). CLARUS needs both to route the shared Mise bot:
  one Telegram bot for many restaurants, where the phone decides which local a
  person belongs to. Always present, never `omitempty`.

## [0.14.0] - 2026-11-03

### Added

- **A Nexus binding can also send media to `media_callback_url`.** When a
  binding without `callback_url` has `media_callback_url` and
  `media_callback_secret` set, every inbound message carrying attachments (a
  Telegram photo, for one) is also queued as a signed webhook delivery
  (`X-Herald-Signature-256`, same payload as `callback_url` forwards, source
  `media_forward`). Nexus still receives the message; a failure to queue the
  forward is logged and does not stop it. URL and secret are re-read from the
  binding at dispatch time, and an empty media secret fails final.

## [0.13.0] - 2026-10-25

### Added

- **New conversations per day, hour and channel for the owner's dashboard.**
  `GET /admin/stats/conversaciones?tenant=&desde=&hasta=&tz=` (admin token)
  answers `{filas: [{dia, hora, canal, nuevas}]}`: conversations created in the
  range, cut into local days and hours of `tz`. CLARUS reads it for the PRESTO
  owner's dashboard (conversations, top channel, out-of-hours share). The range
  is capped at 62 days and `hasta` before `desde` is a 400.

### Fixed

- **Time zones travel inside the binary.** The runtime image (alpine) ships no
  zoneinfo, so `time.LoadLocation` rejected every real zone and the new route
  would have answered 400 to every request. `time/tzdata` is embedded in the
  server package; `tz=Local` and an empty `tz` are a 400 (Postgres used to turn
  `Local` into a 500).

## [0.12.0] - 2026-10-19

### Added

- **Messenger, the fourth channel.** DMs of a Facebook Page both ways, with
  Instagram's signature and handshake. Button postbacks ("Get Started", menu)
  reach the agent as text, and echoes of the Page's own messages are ignored
  so the agent cannot answer itself. There is no `TemplateSender` (pinned by a
  test): nothing is sent outside the 24h window. `pages_messaging` is still in
  App Review, so the emulator (`"canal":"messenger"`) is the path that
  exercises it end to end. Configured with `HERALD_MESSENGER_APP_SECRET`,
  `_VERIFY_TOKEN`, `_GRAPH_BASE_URL` and `_EMULATED_ACCOUNT`.

### Fixed

- **Instagram was missing from the admin UI.** It never made it into the
  channel list or the account hints, so an Instagram account could not be
  created or filtered from the console.

## [0.11.0] - 2026-09-20

### Fixed

- **A failed run left the person with nothing — no fallback, and no error
  either.** Ten inbound Telegram messages from one customer's employee went
  unanswered in mvp between 2026-09-19 01:31 and 2026-09-20 02:56 UTC. Nexus
  had all ten invocations recorded as `error` (kimi-k3 answering 429, the
  model provider's account suspended) while Herald logged no error at all and
  queued no reply, against a binding whose `fallback_message` was configured
  and correct. Two faults stacked on top of each other:

  - **The 502 was laundered into a success.** Nexus registers an invocation
    *before* dispatching it, so the client's 5xx retry can never execute a
    second time: it always lands on the idempotency replay, which answers 200
    with the stored row and no `answer` (astromesh-nexus,
    `internal/server/handlers/invocations.go:245`). Herald read *only*
    `answer`, so it could not tell "the first delivery already replied" from
    "the run failed" — the error vanished and what remained was the
    empty-answer warning, which queues nothing. The client now reads `status`
    as well (`internal/adapters/agentclient/nexus/client.go`,
    `answerStillComing`). The two benign values are `ok` (it already replied)
    and `in_progress` (the original will reply, and replying here would
    double-message the user); everything else is a closed run that produced
    nothing and never will. An unknown status falls on the failure side
    deliberately: a spurious fallback is visible and cheap, silence is not.
  - **The fallback only ever fired for two errors.** It was sent for
    `ErrAgentNotFound` / `ErrAgentForbidden` alone — a test of whether the
    failure is worth retrying, when the fallback answers a different question:
    whether the person who wrote is going to hear anything back. Nothing
    retries an inbound message anyway (`internal/server/inbound_queue.go` logs
    the error and moves on), so the old split spent the fallback on precisely
    the failures a user could best afford. It now goes out for every run
    failure, and the error still propagates: the fallback is for the person,
    the error is for the operator, and the incident produced neither.

- **A message with no text died at the provider with a 400.** A photo, an
  audio, a sticker or the contact someone shares with the identity button
  arrives with `Text` empty; that travelled as `query: ""`, astromesh built an
  empty user turn and the provider rejected the whole request — *"the message
  at position 1 with role 'user' must not be empty"* — so the person got
  nothing. Five messages died that way in mvp on 2026-09-17 and 09-18. The
  worst case is the shared contact, because it is the one mandatory step of
  channel identity: `UpsertIdentity` had already stored the phone number and
  the agent never ran to acknowledge it, so someone handing over their number
  was answered with silence. A message with no text now travels as a short
  bracketed description of what did arrive (`internal/app/receive.go`,
  `consulta`). **This is not attachment support** — the file still dies in
  Herald; what changes is that the agent can *say* it cannot read it.

- **The webchat slug uniqueness fix ships here, not in 0.10.0.** Its bullet
  sits under `[0.10.0]` above, but the commit landed after that release was
  cut, so mvp is getting it now: `channel_accounts_webchat_external_uq`
  (`internal/adapters/store/postgres/migrations/0006_webchat_hilo.sql`) stops
  two tenants from registering the same CLARUS-minted slug.

### Changed

- `MediaAttachment.Kind`'s vocabulary moved up to `domain`
  (`MediaKindImage` / `Audio` / `Video` / `Document`). It lived duplicated in
  the Telegram and Instagram adapters; now that the application layer reads it
  too, the spare copy stops being noise and becomes the chance for emitter and
  reader to differ by one letter with nothing failing. Both adapters point
  their private constants at these. WhatsApp's `msgType*` are deliberately
  left alone: they are Meta's message types, the provider's vocabulary and not
  Herald's.

- **The mvp overlay turns the webchat channel on** (`--enable-webchat`, same
  value as dev, `deploy/overlays/mvp/configmap-patch.yaml`). Without the flag
  a chat link published by CLARUS 1.159.0 in mvp stops answering with no
  error.

## [0.10.0] - 2026-09-14

### Added

- **The webchat channel**, behind `--enable-webchat` / `HERALD_ENABLE_WEBCHAT`
  (off by default; `true` in the dev overlay, `deploy/overlays/dev/configmap-patch.yaml`).
  CLARUS fronts the visitor's browser — Herald never speaks WebSocket to it —
  and reaches the channel through two admin routes
  (`internal/server/handlers_webchat.go`, registered only when the channel is,
  `internal/server/server.go`):

  - `POST /admin/webchat/inbound` (`cuenta`, `visitante`, `texto`) pushes the
    visitor's message onto the same inbound queue every webhook feeds, with a
    generated `channel_message_id` (`messages` is unique on
    `(channel, account_id, channel_message_id)`,
    `internal/adapters/store/postgres/migrations/0004_message_dedupe_per_account.sql:27`).
    An unknown `cuenta` is a synchronous `404` — unlike the WhatsApp emulator,
    where that failure only surfaces later, logged, inside the queue worker.
  - `GET /admin/webchat/hilo?cuenta=&visitante=&desde=` reads the visitor's
    thread back (`postgres.Store.WebchatHilo`, `internal/adapters/store/postgres/admin_reads.go`):
    the visitor's `messages` rows unioned with the agent's `sent` `outbox`
    rows, ordered by when each became visible, capped at 200
    (`maxHilo`, `internal/server/handlers_webchat.go`) and paged with `desde`
    (RFC3339Nano, exclusive).
  - Delivery is a no-op: `SendText`/`SendMedia` return `nil`
    (`internal/adapters/channel/webchat/webchat.go`), so the dispatcher marks
    the outbox row `sent` and that row is what `Hilo` shows — no session
    registry, nothing lost on a restart.

  Two new indexes back both queries — `messages (account_id, external_user,
  created_at)` and a partial `outbox (account_id, recipient, updated_at)
  WHERE status = 'sent'`
  (`internal/adapters/store/postgres/migrations/0006_webchat_hilo.sql`) —
  without them each call scans both tables.

  **`ParseIncoming` rejects every request, and must**: registering the
  adapter is also what opens the generic `POST /webhooks/webchat`, and that
  route checks no signature (there is no provider to sign against). A parser
  that returned messages would turn an unauthenticated route on the public
  internet into an agent trigger; `TestElWebhookDeWebchatNoAcepta`
  (`internal/server/handlers_webhooks_test.go`) is what goes red if that ever
  changes.

  **The agent side of the thread orders by `outbox.updated_at`, not
  `created_at`.** An answer split with `[[+]]` (0.7.4) opens one outbox row
  per fragment, all enqueued together but sent one at a time with a pause
  between them — `created_at` would put every fragment of one answer at the
  same instant, or ahead of a message that took longer to arrive. `updated_at`
  is the moment `MarkSent` ran, which is the moment CLARUS's poll is supposed
  to see it (`domain.HiloMensaje`, `internal/domain/hilo.go`).

### Fixed

- **A webchat slug can no longer belong to two tenants.** Unlike a WhatsApp
  or Telegram `external_id`, a webchat one is a slug CLARUS mints, so the
  plain `(tenant_id, channel, external_id)` UNIQUE let two tenants register
  the same slug — and `GetAccountByExternalID` resolves by `(channel,
  external_id)` alone, so either could resolve the other's inbound message.
  `channel_accounts_webchat_external_uq`, a partial unique index on
  `external_id WHERE channel = 'webchat'`
  (`internal/adapters/store/postgres/migrations/0006_webchat_hilo.sql`),
  closes it: a second tenant's `CreateAccount` on an already-used webchat
  slug now fails instead of silently creating a shadow account.

## [0.9.0] - 2026-09-13

### Added

- **`GET /api/v1/identities/resolve`: which channel address verified a phone.**
  Trusted-sender plane (`X-Herald-Sender-Key`), query `tenant_id`, `channel`,
  `phone` (URL-encoded: a raw `+` arrives as a space). One match is
  `200 {"external_user": "<address>"}`, none is `200 {"external_user": null}`,
  more than one is `409`. CLARUS's gastronómico scheduler uses it to learn a
  person's `direccion_canal` from the identity Telegram verified, so the agent
  no longer needs write access to people. "None" is 200 and not 404 on
  purpose: against a Herald without this route, a 404 must stay an error.

## [0.8.0] - 2026-09-11

### Added

- **The agent now knows which message a Telegram reply quotes.** When someone
  answers with Telegram's "reply", the update carries `reply_to_message`; the
  adapter parses it into `domain.Message.ReplyTo` (`domain.QuotedMessage`:
  `ChannelMessageID` as `chat_id:message_id`, the quoted `text` or `caption`,
  `FromBot`, and `SentAt` in UTC), and `ReceiveMessage` passes it to the agent
  run as the context key `reply_to`:
  `{texto, message_id, del_bot, enviado_el}`.

  Why it exists: with several questions pending, "10" alone does not say which
  one it answers. On 2026-09-10 three quoted replies to three different
  questions ended up recorded against the same one. The CLARUS kiosk auditor
  (template v4) matches the quoted text against the question it sent.

  Three things that do not follow from reading the diff:

  - **The key is always present.** Without a quote it is an untyped `nil`
    (JSON `null`), not missing: `citaParaElAgente` returns `any` and not
    `map[string]any`, because a nil map stored in an interface is not `== nil`.
  - **`del_bot` matters.** Quoting your own message is not answering a
    question, so consumers must check it and not just `reply_to`.
  - **Telegram only.** WhatsApp sends just the quoted message id
    (`context.id`), and Herald does not store outbound ids yet, so `reply_to`
    stays `nil` there and on Instagram.

  No migration: `ReplyTo` is per-message metadata, like `ContactName`, and the
  full update is already in `raw_payload`.

## [0.7.4] - 2026-09-08

### Added

- **An agent answer can now go out as SEVERAL messages, with a pause between
  them**, instead of one block. The agent writes `[[+]]` between messages —
  one LLM call, one `answer` — and `enqueueReply` opens one outbox row per
  fragment (`internal/app/fragmentos.go`).

  **The pause is not a `sleep` and not a goroutine**: it lives in each row's
  `next_retry_at`, which is what `ClaimPending` already reads to decide what
  is due. It costs nothing and it survives a restart — the batch resumes where
  it was instead of losing half an answer.

  Three things that do not follow from reading the diff:

  - **The pause must be >= the poll interval**, because each pass claims
    everything due at once: a shorter pause lands two fragments in the same
    batch and they ship back-to-back, with nothing failing. Hence
    `--outbox-poll-interval` dropping from 2s to 500ms, and a test that goes
    red if anyone inverts that relationship again.
  - **`created_at` is offset one millisecond per fragment.** The dispatcher
    orders by that column and it is the only order there is: with the same
    instant on every row, one delayed pass is enough for two fragments to come
    due together and ship out of order.
  - **If a middle fragment FAILS, ordering breaks**: its retry is 30s away, by
    which time the ones after it have shipped. Accepted knowingly — today a
    failure eats the whole answer — and it is the other reason for the
    `MaxFragmentos` cap.

  Opt-in by prompt, not by configuration: an agent that never writes the
  marker produces one fragment and sends one message, exactly as before.

### Fixed

- `AGENTS.md` said the `Idempotency-Key` toward Nexus was
  `<channel>:<channel_message_id>`. It has carried the account since the
  2026-09-07 fix — the one that stopped messages from being silently eaten.

## [0.7.3] - 2026-09-08

### Fixed

- **No message was ever linked to its conversation**, so
  `GET /admin/conversations/:id/messages` returned nothing for anyone, ever.
  The insert happens *before* the conversation is known — deliberately, so a
  message survives a failure anywhere downstream — and nothing wrote the link
  afterwards: `msg.ConversationID = conv.ID` only mutated the in-memory struct,
  and the existing-conversation path never set it at all. Measured against mvp
  on 2026-09-08: **all 79 stored messages had an empty `conversation_id`, going
  back to the first one on 2026-08-25.** The link is now persisted as soon as
  the conversation is known — before the agent runs when it already exists,
  because a message that made the agent fail is precisely the one worth
  looking at.
- **`last_message_at` was written once, at INSERT, and never again**, so it
  held the conversation's creation time forever: a list sorted by "most recent
  activity" that never reordered. A conversation with messages from four
  different days still reported its first. `TouchConversation` moves it
  forward with `GREATEST`, so two concurrent messages arriving out of order
  cannot push it backwards.

Both failures are logged and never abort: this is bookkeeping for the
conversation view, and withholding a reply the agent already produced would be
a worse bug than losing the link.

## [0.7.2] - 2026-09-07

### Fixed

- **Changing a bot silently ate customer messages, and left no trace
  anywhere.** The idempotency key sent to Nexus was `channel:message_id`, and a
  channel's message id is only unique *within its account* — Telegram restarts
  `message_id` at 1 for every bot. So pointing a deployment at a new bot
  replayed ids Nexus already held; its idempotency check answered 200 with the
  stored row and **no answer**, Herald had nothing to enqueue, and the message
  ended: stored in `messages`, no agent run, no reply, **no log line in any of
  the three systems**. Measured in mvp on 2026-09-07 — of four messages, the
  two whose ids a bot deleted three days earlier had already spent vanished;
  the two with fresh ids answered normally. The account is now part of the key.
  A retry of the same delivery carries the same account, so provider-retry
  safety is unchanged.
- **An empty answer is logged instead of dropped.** Even with unique keys, a
  genuine provider retry still lands on Nexus's replay and still comes back
  without an answer. Herald used to fall straight through to `return nil`, so
  the only evidence of a dropped message was the customer asking why nobody
  wrote back. It is a warning, not an error: on a real retry the first delivery
  already replied.
- **The in-memory store deduped messages without the account**, so it rejected
  what Postgres accepts — `UNIQUE (channel, account_id, channel_message_id)`.
  No test could express two bots on one channel, which is why nothing caught
  any of this. The file already stated exactly this rule for `CreateBinding`
  three lines below.

### Changed

- The comment on `RunRequest.IdempotencyKey` claimed the replay "makes provider
  webhook retries safe end to end". It does not — the retry gets no answer.
  What it makes safe is the agent not running twice.

## [0.7.1] - 2026-09-07

### Fixed

- **Lint was red again, and again it was `misspell` against Spanish.** The
  ignore list added in 0.6.x covered the words of that round; the comments that
  came with Instagram and the Telegram identity brought new ones —
  `comparte`→`compare`, `coordinar`→`coordinator`, `previos`→`previous`. Same
  treatment: the words are ignored, the linter is not.
- The four genuine issues the noise was burying are closed: one over-long line
  in `main.go`, two modernizations (`range` over an int, `strings.SplitSeq`),
  and a test helper whose channel parameter always received
  `ChannelTelegram` — the four callers are the contact-button cases, which are
  Telegram-only, so the parameter suggested a generality that does not exist.

## [0.7.0] - 2026-09-07

### Added

- **Instagram, the third channel (S1).** DMs and stories both ways. Instagram is
  Meta, so it inherits WhatsApp's signature and handshake shape; what it does
  not inherit are templates, and that absence is pinned by a test — there is no
  `TemplateSender`. The emulator stopped being welded to the WhatsApp adapter,
  which was the precondition for everything else: `instagram_manage_messages` is
  still in Meta's App Review, so until it clears, the emulator is the only path
  that exercises the channel end to end.
- **Telegram can tell who is writing.** `external_user` is a `chat.id` there,
  not a phone, so the five ARGOS verticals that resolve a person by looking up
  `{{ sender }}` in their roster found nobody — four of them degraded **in
  silence**, treating a known customer as a stranger. The only path that is not
  inventing authentication is the `request_contact` button: the person taps it
  and Telegram attaches the number of *their* account. A `contact` counts only
  when `contact.user_id == from.id` — without that comparison anyone could
  impersonate anyone with two taps.
- **A proactive send can name the account it goes out from.** `SendRequest`
  gains an optional `AccountID`; empty keeps `FindAccount`'s old behaviour, and
  that backward compatibility is half the design — it ships before its callers,
  with no coordinated cutover. Until now a tenant with two centurias sent every
  notice from whichever number was registered first: 200 OK, no error anywhere,
  and the only one who noticed was the customer getting a message from a number
  they did not recognise. Membership is validated, and an account that exists
  but belongs to another tenant is indistinguishable from one that does not —
  `/send-on-behalf` authenticates with the trusted sender key, which speaks for
  any tenant.

### Fixed

- **A conversation stopped answering once its agent no longer existed.** Herald
  routed every existing conversation to the agent stored on its row,
  unconditionally. The rule is deliberate — it holds a handoff together across
  messages — but it was missing the one limit that matters: it holds *while that
  agent exists*. CLARUS puts the deployment id inside the agent name, so
  replacing a deployment mints a new name and unpublishes the old one; from then
  on every conversation created earlier got a 404 and the person got the
  fallback, forever. Whoever wrote in for the first time came through the
  binding and worked fine, so the deployment looked healthy while it was dead
  precisely for the people already engaged. `rescueConversation` catches the 404
  and retries with the binding's entry agent. Measured in dev on 2026-09-01.
- **Instagram's env vars were documented and never wired.** S1 documented
  `HERALD_INSTAGRAM_*` in the README and nobody put them in `deploy/`, so the
  channel stayed inert: `/webhooks/instagram` answered 404 while
  `/webhooks/whatsapp` answered 403. Without them the adapter does not register
  at all. It is the "documented but inert" pattern this ecosystem already has
  written down for Centuria, repeated.
- **A turn's timeout ceiling could be declared but not configured.**

## [0.6.0] - 2026-08-28

### Added

- **Telegram, the second real channel.** Text and media both ways: inbound
  `Update` parsing, `sendMessage`/`sendPhoto`/`sendDocument`/`sendVideo`/
  `sendAudio` by public link, and `getFile` resolving an inbound `file_id` to
  bytes. A bot registers itself: creating its channel account calls
  `setWebhook`, so CLARUS deploys a Telegram Centuria through the same
  `POST /admin/accounts` it already calls for WhatsApp, with no change on its
  side.

  The point was never Telegram. It was making the third channel cheap, with
  Instagram DM and Messenger next. Telegram earned the slot precisely because
  those two are Meta-shaped like WhatsApp: testing the port with them would
  have passed while leaving every hidden WhatsApp-ism in place. Telegram has no
  Meta HMAC, no `hub.challenge` handshake, no 24h window, no approved
  templates, and — uniquely — identifies the account OUTSIDE the payload.

  Measured result: adding Instagram DM now touches a new package, the channel
  constant, config/wiring and the manifests. It does NOT touch the webhook
  handler, the dispatcher, or `internal/ports`.

- **`ports.SignatureHeaderNamer`** — a channel declares which header carries its
  signature. The handler used to hold a list of provider header names in the
  layer that documents itself as owning HTTP concerns only, and every new
  channel appended to it. Telegram's is `X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token`.

- **`ports.WebhookRegistrar`** — for providers that must be TOLD where to
  deliver. Meta's webhook is configured once per app in its dashboard;
  Telegram's `setWebhook` is per bot, and a bot nobody registers receives
  nothing while looking perfectly healthy. `CreateAccount` registers BEFORE
  writing the row: the reverse leaves an account that looks fine and never
  receives, which is the invisible failure. A webhook left pointing at a row
  that was never written is harmless — deliveries resolve to no account and are
  dropped with a log.

- **`POST /webhooks/:channel/:cuenta`** — the account travels in the URL for
  channels whose payload cannot name it (a Telegram `Update` names the chat,
  never the bot). The handler stamps `AccountExternalID` only on messages the
  parser left EMPTY: stamping unconditionally would mask a parse bug and
  resolve a message to the wrong tenant.

- **`HERALD_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`** (generic, not Telegram-specific — every channel
  that registers a webhook needs it) and **`TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`**, the
  process-level `secret_token` echoed back on every delivery. Absent secret →
  the adapter is not registered → its webhook is a 404, the same closed-door
  rule every other credential here follows.

### Fixed

- **Inbound dedupe scoped by account (migration 0004), closing a silent
  cross-tenant message loss.** `messages` was `UNIQUE (channel,
  channel_message_id)`, which held only because WhatsApp's `wamid.*` is unique
  across phone numbers. Telegram is the first channel whose provider id is
  unique only PER ACCOUNT: in a private chat `chat.id` is the user's GLOBAL id —
  the same number for every bot that person writes to — and `message_id`
  restarts at 1 per bot conversation. So the same user writing to two tenants'
  bots produced the same key, the second insert was absorbed as a duplicate, and
  the second tenant's agent never ran: no log at that level, webhook already
  answered 200.

  The key is now `(channel, account_id, channel_message_id)` — per-account
  dedupe, which is the semantics that was always meant. WhatsApp is unaffected.
  Prefixing the bot id in the adapter was not merely worse, it was impossible:
  `ParseIncoming` does not know the account, the handler stamps it.

- **A Bot API refusal is no longer uniformly permanent.** `DownloadMedia`
  converted every `ok:false` to `ports.ErrMediaUnavailable` — attachment dropped
  forever — including `429` (flood control) and `401` (token rotating). The
  WhatsApp adapter already excludes exactly those (`graph.go:36-56`), with the
  written argument that treating 429 as permanent makes a burst of inbound
  photos self-discard on their first attempt. Telegram now uses the same
  criterion.

- **The bot token no longer reaches an error message.** It rides in every
  request path (`/bot<token>/METHOD`) and in the file-download URL, and
  `net/http` embeds the full URL in the `*url.Error` of any transport failure —
  a string the outbox persists verbatim into `LastError` and serves unmasked.
  Every network error path now unwraps to the inner error first, and a test goes
  red if the token reappears.

### Changed

- `VERSION` jumps 0.4.0 → 0.6.0. The 0.5.0 entry below shipped without its
  `VERSION` bump, so no `:0.5.0` image was ever published; renumbering now would
  be worse than the gap, since `:X.Y.Z` is immutable and must never be
  republished with different content.

## [0.5.0] - 2026-08-26

### Added

- **More than one emulated WhatsApp number at a time, and an account can
  declare itself one.** Until now `esEmulado` compared the account's
  `ExternalID` against a single configured string, so an environment could
  stand in for exactly ONE line: the second vertical that wanted to be tested
  had to take the emulator away from the first. Measured in `dev`, where `agro`
  held it — which is why the confirmation-gate fix for `cobranzas` was never
  exercised.

  Two ways to say a line is a stand-in, and one gate above both:

  1. **The account says so** — `channel_accounts.emulated` (migration 0003).
     This is the one that scales: which line is a stand-in is a property of one
     tenant's deployment, and whoever creates the account knows it. It travels
     in the `DO UPDATE` next to the credentials, so a redeploy that changes its
     mind converges instead of freezing on whatever was created first.
  2. **The configuration names them** — `HERALD_WHATSAPP_EMULATED_NUMBER` goes
     from one string to a comma-separated list. It stays because it needs no
     database write: an operator can stand in for an already-registered line
     with nobody else in the loop. `New` still takes a single string, so no
     caller and no overlay passing one number changes.
  3. **The gate** — the environment must have the emulator on for either to
     count. `Emulated` is a database row, so it travels: a dump restored into
     production, a tenant cloned from a demo, a caller sending the field by
     mistake. Without this cut, any of those would silently swallow every
     message a real customer was meant to receive, and nothing would look
     broken — the send returns nil. With it, production (which configures no
     number) ignores the column entirely.

- **`GET /admin/emulator/outbox?cuenta=`** narrows the outbox to one line. The
  ring is shared, so two verticals under test interleave in it: reading the
  last message without filtering hands back whichever one answered last. That
  is a measured misread, not a hypothetical.

## [0.4.0] - 2026-08-26

### Fixed

- **A channel account now converges instead of colliding.**
  `POST /admin/accounts` inserts `ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, channel,
  external_id) DO UPDATE` and answers **200** with the surviving row's id (201
  when it really created one), refreshing the stored credentials on the way.
  It used to be a plain `INSERT`, so the unique breach surfaced as a 500.

  An account is a shared resource: one tenant has one WhatsApp number, and
  everything that sends through it wants the same row. The 500 made the most
  ordinary sequence impossible — tear a deployment down (which keeps the
  account on purpose) and the next one on that same number could never be
  created, with no way forward but deleting the account by hand.

### Changed

- **A duplicate binding is a 409, not a 500**, and its body names the way out
  ("delete the existing binding before creating another"). Deliberately NOT
  converged like the account above: a binding carries one `entry_agent`, so
  adopting the row already there would silently hand this caller's traffic to
  someone else's agent. `domain.ErrAlreadyExists` is the signal; only
  `CreateBinding` returns it.

## [0.3.1] - 2026-08-25

### Changed

- mvp turns the emulated WhatsApp number on, so the product flow can be
  validated before prod — which is what that environment is for. It must be
  cleared the day mvp takes real traffic; the overlay says so.

## [0.3.0] - 2026-08-25

### Added

- **An emulated WhatsApp number** (`--whatsapp-emulated-number` /
  `HERALD_WHATSAPP_EMULATED_NUMBER`, empty = off). One phone-number-id stops
  going to Meta: its sends are recorded in memory and reported delivered,
  inbound messages can be injected through `POST /admin/emulator/inbound`, and
  `GET /admin/emulator/outbox` shows what the agent replied. Every other
  account still goes to the Graph API, and the public webhook still verifies
  Meta's signature.

  It exists because a product flow could not be exercised end to end without a
  Meta account. The `echo` channel already covers "run the pipeline with no
  provider", but it is a different channel: it does not exercise WhatsApp,
  which is what ARGOS uses for campaigns and templates.

  Both routes sit behind the admin token and neither is registered without a
  configured number — injecting an inbound message IS invoking an agent, so it
  must not be a weaker door than the account CRUD.

### Changed

- **`--agent-run-timeout` (default 120s, was a hardcoded 30s.)** It has to
  outlast the WHOLE agent turn, not one LLM round-trip: an agent that calls
  tools does several. Measured with a real collections agent, closing a payment
  plan took 35s over four tool steps — Herald cancelled the request, Nexus
  aborted with `close invocation: begin: context canceled`, and the person got
  NOTHING, with no retry (a client timeout is not a 5xx).

- The WhatsApp adapter now registers when an emulated number is set even
  without an app secret. Without that, no adapter is registered and every
  outbox entry fails permanently — emulating would have emulated nothing.

## [0.2.0] - 2026-08-12

The three enablers a caller needs to own a WhatsApp conversation itself,
instead of handing it to a Nexus agent. Written for ARGOS (CLARUS's kiosk
auditor), but none of it names that caller.

### Added

- **Template sends.** `OutboxPayload` carries a `TemplatePayload`, the send API
  accepts it over HTTP, and the WhatsApp adapter emits body parameters as Graph
  `components`. Without a template there is no way to open a conversation
  outside WhatsApp's 24-hour window, so a service that asks first — rather than
  answering — could not start at all.
- **Per-binding webhook forwarding.** A binding can carry `callback_url` and
  `callback_secret` in its `config` JSONB, and having a `callback_url` opts the
  whole conversation out of Nexus: inbound messages are POSTed as JSON signed
  with HMAC-SHA256 (`internal/adapters/webhookclient`) through the same outbox
  as every other send, so a forward inherits the retry budget instead of being
  a fire-and-forget HTTP call on the receive path.
- **Incoming media reaches the webhook.** A new optional `MediaDownloader` port
  (WhatsApp already satisfies it) downloads the attachment and rides along
  base64 in the forward payload, capped at 8 MiB — the limit is anchored by a
  test against the literal, because the 16 MiB it replaced peaked the process
  heap at ~124 MiB while the same process had to keep answering Meta.
- **Webhook-only bindings in the console.** A binding that forwards can be
  created and edited without naming a Nexus agent, its callback config is
  validated on write, masked on read, and **merged** rather than replaced.
- Apache-2.0, the same license as Nexus.

### Fixed

- **The dispatcher re-resolves `callback_url` at delivery time**, not just the
  secret. A queued forward used a snapshot from enqueue time, so clearing or
  retargeting a callback left in-flight messages going to the old URL.
- **The webhook client fails closed and stays put**: it does not follow
  redirects, an empty secret is an error rather than an unsigned POST, and the
  response body is drained so connections are reused.
- **A dropped attachment is no longer indistinguishable from a message that
  never had one.** Both arrived at the webhook as a payload with no media, so a
  receiver could not tell "the kiosk sent no photo" from "we failed to fetch
  the photo it sent".
- `send` no longer leaks storage errors to the caller, and rejects NUL bytes
  before they reach the outbox.

## [0.1.0] - 2026-08-06

First release. Everything below is what the initial cut contains, so the
sections describe the service rather than a delta against a previous version.

### Added

- Communications gateway: inbound channel webhooks invoke agents through Nexus
  (`POST /api/v1/agents/:name/run`) with a stable `session_id` per channel
  conversation, and Nexus-originated proactive sends ride the same Postgres
  outbox as agent replies.
- WhatsApp Cloud API adapter: `hub.challenge` handshake, `X-Hub-Signature-256`
  verification, text/image/audio/video/document parsing, Graph API sends,
  template sends and media download.
- Echo development channel (behind `--enable-echo`) plus contract stubs for
  telegram, webchat and smtp.
- Operator plane at `/admin` behind `X-Admin-Token`, with channel-account
  credentials AES-GCM sealed at rest and masked (`•••` + last 4) on read.
- Embedded operator console at `/ui/` (React + Vite in `ui/`): overview,
  conversations with their message thread, an outbox monitor showing each
  entry's retry budget, and routing-rule and channel-account CRUD.
- `POST /api/v1/messages/send-on-behalf` behind `X-Herald-Sender-Key`
  (`--trusted-sender-key`), for a caller that dispatches for every tenant and
  therefore names the tenant in the body. Its own route group with its own
  header, so a tenant's `X-Herald-Key` cannot reach a route that trusts
  `tenant_id`.
- `pkg/heraldclient`: stdlib-only public client of the send API, for Nexus to
  import.
- Deployment: kustomize base plus dev and mvp overlays, ArgoCD Applications and
  Image Updater configs, GHCR publishing, and the `/deploy-dev` and
  `/deploy-mvp` release commands.
- `deploy/bootstrap.sh <dev|mvp>`: prepares a channel namespace in one command
  — the four out-of-git Secrets, then the Application and Image Updater —
  and refuses to touch `herald-secrets` once it exists, because `enc-key`
  seals every stored channel credential and there is no re-encryption path.

### Fixed

- The container image had never built: `.dockerignore` excluded the
  `go:embed`ed migrations, so the Go stage failed on
  `pattern migrations/0001_init.sql: no matching files found`. This broke
  `make docker-build` and the compose quickstart alike.
- The Lint workflow had never passed: `make lint` invoked a bare
  `golangci-lint`, which no CI runner provides. Tools are now pinned and
  installed into `bin/`.
- An exported `NODE_ENV=development` leaked React's development build into the
  console's production bundle (454 kB against 219 kB). The build script pins
  the mode, so its output no longer depends on whose shell ran it.
- `seedAdminReads` stamped a test row one minute in the future, which lands
  inside every `created_at >= now() - N days` window — including the zero-day
  one `TestStatsAggregates` asserts is empty.
